headline: CISA: Hackers targeted over 100 US water systems in July
summary: Cyberattacks exploiting AI tools and targeting industrial control systems have hit more than 100 water facilities nationwide, CISA confirms.
details: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has confirmed that over 100 internet-exposed systems within the U.S. water and wastewater sector were targeted by cyberattacks in July. This wave of attacks is part of a broader trend of intrusions targeting American critical infrastructure.

These attacks primarily focused on programmable logic controllers (PLCs), which are essential for managing physical systems in water providers, energy sectors, and other critical infrastructure. Manufacturers like Rockwell, Schneider Electric, and Siemens have been identified as targets.

Notably, some of these cyberattacks are reportedly leveraging AI tools to develop scripts that exploit vulnerabilities in Siemens PLCs. While most intrusions have had minimal impact on water supplies, they have caused disruptions and outages as incident responders investigate.

In some cases, hackers were able to modify PLCs to disable shutdown processes and alarms, potentially creating unsafe conditions without operators being alerted. Many affected communities are in rural areas where such disruptions can have a significant impact.

U.S. intelligence agencies suspect Iran is behind these opportunistic attacks, possibly as retaliation for the ongoing conflict between the U.S. and Israel against Iran. However, a definitive attribution has not been made.

The incidents raise broader concerns about the cybersecurity and resilience of the nation's critical infrastructure, with past warnings highlighting potential threats from state-sponsored actors like China and Russia targeting similar systems.

headline_marked: [[Z.ai]] is the AI lab behind the mysterious Ox Alpha model
headline: Z.ai is the AI lab behind the mysterious Ox Alpha model
summary: The new open-weight AI model Ox Alpha, which has been topping leaderboards, is confirmed to be from Z.ai. Its weights will be released on Wednesday.
details: Speculation is over: Z.ai, the company behind the GLM series of AI models, has been confirmed as the creator of the mysterious Ox Alpha model. The model was anonymously launched on OpenRouter and quickly rose to the top of benchmarks and leaderboards.

Ox Alpha is described as a reasoning model specifically designed for coding tasks, sustained agentic work, and production workloads. It is also suited for long-horizon software engineering, complex reasoning, and workflows that integrate text with visual context.

Z.ai announced that the weights for Ox Alpha will be released on Wednesday, allowing developers to build upon the model. This release follows Z.ai's recent launch of GLM-5.3 earlier this month, which has shown competitive performance against models from companies like Anthropic.

The emergence of capable and affordable AI models from China, such as Ox Alpha, poses a growing challenge to established frontier model companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, potentially capturing significant market share.
